searchText: <@539495253418180618> regarding builder api latency, with electra the payloads will increase quite a bit due to execution requests, having a ssz serialized list of those inside a json body does not make sense to me on the CL side, but we can adopt SSZ as proposed in https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/104. A hard fork would be a good opportunity to roll this out. The sentiment from builders and sidecar implementers from the mev-boost call seemed supportive. Re-posting this here to get some feedback from CL devs. has this been measured? how much of the latency is network, or CPU, or etc? It's a difference scenario than typical engine API since it's not local anymore SSZ has its appeals anyway, but I guess, at this point it's clear timing games are going to happen. So my concern is anything here just is a zero-sum game moving latency budget back to the relays/builders So is it worth it? there are few benchmarks here https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/53, we also saw really good latency improvements switching from json to ssz is the block apis and that's a local connection Okay, stipulated, SSZ does seem significantly faster my main concerns is that this disproportionally affects solo stakers and low bandwidth nodes also we receive the blinded block from vc as ssz now since we use that by default and have to convert it to json when submitting to builder, but the beacon node here is really just a passthrough Yeah, in general I'm not opposed to SSZ, to be clear I'm just ... hm. It's engineering effort to change, and I'm not sure it benefits the CLs. Maybe. I can't tell what's the effort for this on every client, in Lodestar is very low, also the CL only implements the client side Maybe, but the does-it-benefit-the-CLs is the main concern I have. That is, along these lines I'll maybe spell it out more clearly: one possible scenario is, the relays still want to serve validators because it does profit them to do so, but they know solo stakers have `n` additional milliseconds (it's a distribution, etc, etc) of total end-to-end transmission time (accounting for bandwidth and latency) But they still need to send out the block + blobs at the same time, so it means they move everything up a bit. Because we know for sure that, see above, the timing games are already happening. It's already playing against deadlines So the latency + bandwidth + CPU usage effect of different encodings just becomes one more input to the game It's not just, is this in isolation an engineering improvement/optimization. It's a question of how it affects the system as a whole against players with misaligned interests Not sure I can answer that, but I get what you mean And, in general, yeah, the Nimbus VC/BN prefer SSZ here too for the blinded beacon APIs I might be biased as well as JSON de/serialization in JS is painfully slow and hard to optimize I mean, I agree. Any time I see our JSON code I just give up on performance generally speaking it's full of buffering and copying because of unknown field ordering etc But my question is different, it's do the relays and builders have any incentive not to just take the gains from this and eat the profits For something CLs spend any resources at all doing that might happen, although we have a strict timeout on getHeader requests on the CL side, and the majority of latency benefits happen when you submit the blinded block yeah i think in any case having SSZ support standardized would be really valuable just need to get deployed in mev-boost and CL clients made a note to bring up on next ACDC https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1178#issuecomment-2405638130 well and relayers (which is the most important) but those are just a small set of known entities

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
<@539495253418180618> regarding builder api latency, with electra the payloads will increase quite a bit due to execution requests, having a ssz serialized list of those inside a json body does not make sense to me on the CL side, but we can adopt SSZ as proposed in https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/104. A hard fork would be a good opportunity to roll this out. The sentiment from builders and sidecar implementers from the mev-boost call seemed supportive.

Re-posting this here to get some feedback from CL devs.

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: has this been measured? how much of the latency is network, or CPU, or etc?

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: It's a difference scenario than typical engine API since it's not local anymore

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: SSZ has its appeals anyway, but I guess, at this point it's clear timing games are going to happen. So my concern is anything here just is a zero-sum game moving latency budget back to the relays/builders

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: So is it worth it?

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: there are few benchmarks here https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/issues/53, we also saw really good latency improvements switching from json to ssz is the block apis and that's a local connection

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Okay, stipulated, SSZ does seem significantly faster

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: my main concerns is that this disproportionally affects solo stakers and low bandwidth nodes

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: also we receive the blinded block from vc as ssz now since we use that by default and have to convert it to json when submitting to builder, but the beacon node here is really just a passthrough

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Yeah, in general I'm not opposed to SSZ, to be clear

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: I'm just ... hm. It's engineering effort to change, and I'm not sure it benefits the CLs. Maybe.

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: I can't tell what's the effort for this on every client, in Lodestar is very low, also the CL only implements the client side

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Maybe, but the does-it-benefit-the-CLs is the main concern I have. That is, along these lines

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: But they still need to send out the block + blobs at the same time, so it means they move everything up a bit.

excerpts.author: tersec

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: So the latency + bandwidth + CPU usage effect of different encodings just becomes one more input to the game

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: It's not just, is this in isolation an engineering improvement/optimization. It's a question of how it affects the system as a whole against players with misaligned interests

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: Not sure I can answer that, but I get what you mean

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: And, in general, yeah, the Nimbus VC/BN prefer SSZ here too

excerpts.author: tersec
